name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,720

clue.text: An element of Spooner's naked wash?

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of neighbouring words, so his name signals that swap

blocks.note: naked is raw and to wash is to clean; swapping the opening sounds R and CL gives claw-reen

explanation.surface: A question about some part of the way the Reverend Spooner bathed in the nude.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the R of raw and the CL of clean and, said in a non-rhotic British accent, you get claw-reen, the halogen CHLORINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Chlorine is a chemical element, a halogen gas with atomic number seventeen.

clue.text: Requests a reserved section for VIP

indicators.note: a section is a part cut from something larger, so the answer is a run of letters inside the clue

blocks.note: the run of letters spans the end of the first word, the whole of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Someone books a roped-off area for an important guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserved section' reads like seating set aside; in fact 'reserved' is part of the letter string and 'section' alone signals the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was a Russian emperor, and the word is now used loosely for any powerful bigwig or very important person.

clue.text: Rovers’ hero tackling player of Wanderers

indicators.note: to tackle is to get to grips with, so one piece wraps itself around another

blocks.note: Roy of the Rovers was a long-running British comic-strip footballer
a player in a team is one of its men

explanation.surface: A football report: the Rovers star makes a tackle on a Wolves (Wanderers) player.
explanation.walkthrough: Roy Race of 'Roy of the Rovers' is the classic British comic-strip footballer. Wanderers is a common football club name, but here it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romany people are traditionally nomadic travellers, so the name stands for a group of wanderers.

clue.text: Busy person, with twist of fate, produces energy drink

indicators.note: a twist turns and contorts something, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a busy person is a busy bee
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A hard-working person, in an ironic turn of fortune, comes up with a new sports drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy drink' suggests a modern caffeinated can; the answer is an old-fashioned restorative broth.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef tea is a hot meaty broth traditionally given to invalids to restore strength, a drink for building energy.

clue.text: Temporarily pause Parliament in favour of unprincipled character

blocks.note: pro means for, in favour of
a rogue is a dishonest, unprincipled person

explanation.surface: A political complaint: suspending Parliament to benefit some scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the 2019 controversy when Boris Johnson's government suspended the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To prorogue is the formal term for discontinuing a session of a legislature without dissolving it.

clue.text: The ups and downs of many a London commuter?

definitions.text: The ups and downs of many a London commuter?

blocks.note: surface reading: the good and bad times in a commuter's life
setter's reading: the moving staircases that literally carry Underground travellers up and down

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ups and downs' is an idiom for fluctuating fortunes; read literally it is the machinery carrying people between street and platform on the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving staircases in Tube stations carry commuters upward and downward every day, literally their ups and downs.

clue.text: Operatic lead is getting on with performance finally

indicators.note: finally points to what comes at the very end, so only a closing letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
someone getting on in years is old
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: An opera star is ageing, though her final performance still lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like a description of the singer's career; it is the title-role heroine herself.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the heroine of Wagner's opera Tristan und Isolde, a leading soprano role.

clue.text: So, these tenors transformed Madchester band

indicators.note: something transformed has been changed in form, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: all thirteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A group of tenors has reinvented itself as an indie rock act.
explanation.walkthrough: Madchester was the late-1980s Manchester music scene mixing indie rock and rave culture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stone Roses were one of the defining groups of the Manchester indie-dance scene, alongside the Happy Mondays.

clue.text: See 8
Fundamentally, rock and roll comprises nothing but loud noise

indicators.note: fundamentally means at the base or root, so only the first letters of the words are kept
to comprise is to include, so one piece sits inside the others

blocks.note: the opening letters of the three words
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A cynic's view: at heart, rock and roll is just a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing but loud noise' reads as one dismissive phrase; 'nothing' is the letter inside and 'but' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A roar is a deep, loud sound, like a lion's call or a crowd's shout.

clue.text: Ring road in pleasant surroundings is within budget

indicators.note: in places one thing within another, so one piece is enclosed by a larger one

blocks.note: a ring is round like the letter O
RD is the abbreviation for road
affable means pleasant and friendly; it surrounds the other pieces

explanation.surface: A ring road set in attractive countryside came in on budget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pleasant surroundings' looks like scenery; it is the word for pleasant, wrapped around the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something affordable has a price people can manage, so it falls inside what they can spend.

clue.text: Vivid railway worker's uniform

blocks.note: live can mean bright and glowing, as in live coals
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A train employee wears a brightly coloured uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Railway worker's' looks like one phrase; the split comes after 'railway', leaving 'worker's uniform' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery is the distinctive dress worn by servants or employees of a household or company.

clue.text: Making sense of cutback taking place in gin supply

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction, so the letters run the other way
to take something in is to hold it, so one piece goes inside another
supply read as supple, bendy and flexible, so the letters bend into a new order

blocks.note: to axe is to cut; the second half of the word is the reversal signal
PL is the abbreviation for place
taken as written
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Analysing a fall in the supply of gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutback' is one word in the surface but splits into a cut and a reversal signal; 'supply' is read as the adjective supple, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Explaining something is clarifying it, making it understandable to someone else.

clue.text: One out to deeply impress uninhibited Penge party-goer

indicators.note: read as 'un-inhibited', with the bounds removed, so the outermost letters drop away and the inside is kept

blocks.note: the inner letters of the place name; Penge is a district of south London
a raver is a lively partygoer

explanation.surface: A wild clubber from Penge sets out to make a big impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deeply impress' sounds like trying to wow people; literally it is cutting a design into a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraver carves or etches marks into metal, wood or stone, pressing an image deep into it.

clue.text: Criminal serves sandwiches quietly for evening gathering at church

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted into a new order
a sandwich holds a filling between its slices, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A felon quietly hands round sandwiches at an evening church social.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' is a verb, not food on a plate; 'Criminal' is not a person but the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Vespers is the traditional evening prayer service in Christian churches.

clue.text: Blanked out as wine took effect

blocks.note: red is a type of wine
a drug or drink that took effect acted

explanation.surface: Someone passed out once the wine kicked in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blanked out' suggests losing consciousness; it means censored with black bars, as in a document.
explanation.definitionFit: A redacted document has sensitive passages obscured or removed before publication.

clue.text: Changes statement claiming success of divinity course?

blocks.note: RE is religious education, a British school subject
'it works' is what you say when something succeeds

explanation.surface: A theology course alters its brochure boasting how well it does.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for religious education, the subject taught in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: To rework something is to revise or alter it, so the third-person form matches the verb.

clue.text: King leads fight with tense English ex-Chancellor

indicators.note: to lead is to go in front, so this piece comes first in the line

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
a war is a fight
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
ENG is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A monarch leads a battle alongside a nervous former English finance minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective describing the minister; it is the grammar term. Kwasi Kwarteng was UK Chancellor of the Exchequer for a few weeks in 2022.
explanation.definitionFit: Kwarteng held the post of Chancellor of the Exchequer, Britain's finance minister, before being sacked.

clue.text: Lacking guile and disastrously two down hosting the French

indicators.note: something gone disastrously has been wrecked, so the letters come out jumbled
a host takes guests in, so one piece holds another inside it

blocks.note: the answer to the clue at 2 down
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: Someone naive goes disastrously two goals down while entertaining French visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two down' reads as a losing score; it is a cross-reference to the answer at 2 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless describes someone simple and sincere, without cunning or deceit.

clue.text: Sicilian perhaps admitting to defamation

blocks.note: an admission begins 'I did it', so someone admitting says I
slander is spoken defamation

explanation.surface: A Sicilian, perhaps a Mafioso, owns up to libelling someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' warns that Sicilian is only one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicily is an island, so a Sicilian is one example of an island inhabitant.

clue.text: NASA's Deep Space Center boosted careers

indicators.note: the centre of a phrase is its inside, so the letters are found within the words
boosted means pushed upward, and in a down clue going up runs the letters backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters from the end of the first word through to the start of the third

explanation.surface: A NASA deep-space facility gave a lift to people's jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Careers' looks like a plural noun for jobs; it is the verb meaning rushes headlong.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to move swiftly and wildly, so careers and speeds are synonymous verbs.

clue.text: Treat former-PM with contempt and consternation

blocks.note: to dis is slang for to treat with disrespect
completes the phrase 'treat with contempt' that the first block stands for; it adds no letters
Theresa May was UK Prime Minister from 2016 to 2019

explanation.surface: Mocking a former Prime Minister is greeted with scorn and alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treat with contempt' is a single slang word; the definition is the last word only.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay is a feeling of shock and distress, close in sense to alarmed bewilderment.

clue.text: Upset as a result of cover-up over a long period

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters bottom to top
one piece placed over another covers it, so it closes around the other

blocks.note: a lid is a cover
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone is distressed because a scandal was hushed up for years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover-up' reads as a scandal; it splits into a cover and a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To derail a plan is to throw it off course, which is one sense of upsetting it.

clue.text: Unclear VAR arrangement results in facetious swearing

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things into a fresh order, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; VAR is football's video assistant referee

explanation.surface: A murky video-referee decision has fans cursing.
explanation.walkthrough: Dictionaries list a jocular sense, 'pardon my vernacular', for crude language.
explanation.definitionFit: The vernacular is everyday speech, and is humorously used to mean coarse or profane language.

clue.text: You heard expression of disapproval about short skirt

indicators.note: what is heard is only its sound, so a word stands for a letter that sounds the same

blocks.note: tut is a clicking sound of disapproval
the letter's name sounds like this word

explanation.surface: You were overheard tutting at a skimpy skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the second sound first; the tut comes before the letter in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is a ballerina's short, stiff, layered skirt that sticks out from the waist.

clue.text: The fourth Doctor W's memorial?

blocks.note: Tom Baker played the fourth Doctor; this is his first name
the remaining part of the name: Doctor W stands for Doctor Who, and the actor's surname is cut to its initial

explanation.surface: A question about a monument to the fourth Doctor Who.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor W is Doctor Who, the BBC science-fiction series; its fourth lead actor was Tom Baker, cut down to first name and initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomb is a grave or monument commemorating the dead, so it serves as a memorial.

clue.text: Nude dancing clubs entertained one popularly sitting in the corner

definitions.text: one popularly sitting in the corner

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so they land in a new order
to entertain guests is to have them in, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Strip clubs put on a show for a lone figure sitting in the corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' looks like nightclubs, but it is the card suit; the cornered figure is the schoolroom dunce in a pointed cap.
explanation.definitionFit: In popular imagery a slow pupil was made to sit in the classroom corner wearing a conical cap.

clue.text: Delivery from trend-setting crew - street clothes?

indicators.note: to clothe is to wrap in garments, so one piece wraps around the others

blocks.note: hip means fashionable
a crew is made up of men
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A fashionable gang's street-wear range has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like a noun for garments; it is the verb, the street wrapping the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipment is a consignment of goods sent out, a load that is delivered.
